newsitem.title: SPAIN: Zaragozano up nearly 15 pct on loan deal.
newsitem.headline: Zaragozano up nearly 15 pct on loan deal.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Banco Zaragozano jumped nearly 15 percent on Monday, benefiting from news it was in a deal with leading retailer El Corte Ingles to provide consumer loans, analysts said.
At 1000 GMT, shares in the group rose 555 pesetas, or 14.98 percent, to 4,260 pesetas while the Ibex index of 35 leading shares rose 80.17 points, or 1.21 percent, to 6,693.39.
Under the deal, Zaragozano will provide customer loans at stores of El Corte Ingles. The three-year loans will have a nominal rate of 8.50 percent and can be extended by one year.
But although the deal was positive, it alone did not account for the dramatic share price rise, analysts and dealers said.
"On its own, the deal doesn't justify a rise of 15 percent," an analyst said.
Alejandro Ruira, analyst at AB Asesores brokerage, said "We are in a bourse that is trending higher and perhaps the mid-size banks have been left behind in the rally."
Another dealer added that the share was fairly illiquid.

But analysts noted that Banco Zaragozano was valued above the market, with a price to earnings ratio of 16 to 19, compared with a sector average of 13.3, in part due to intermittent talk that it is a takeover target.
